title: This Fish Chokes Sharks With Slime in Half a Second

scenes.text: This fish chokes sharks with slime in half a second.
The hagfish. A shark bites it, and its mouth and gills fill with slime instantly.
Scientists filmed it in 2011. Sharks and eels that bit one gagged, convulsed and fled.
The hagfish just kept eating. Not a scratch on it.
In 2017, a truck carrying 7,500 pounds of them crashed in Oregon. Slime buried the highway.
It even ties itself in a knot to scrape its own slime off. Half a second. Shark gone.

description:
A hagfish can fill a shark's mouth and gills with slime in less than half a second.
In 2011, deep-sea cameras off New Zealand filmed sharks, conger eels and other predators biting hagfish, then gagging, convulsing and fleeing, while the hagfish carried on feeding unharmed. In 2017 a truck carrying 7,500 pounds of hagfish overturned on US 101 in Oregon and buried the road and a car in slime. Hagfish clear their own slime by tying themselves in a knot.
What's the grossest animal defence you know? Comment below.
first_comment: Hagfish have no jaws and no real spine, and they've been around for about 300 million years. Their slime threads are being studied for bulletproof fabric. Would you eat one? In Korea it's a delicacy.
